//: Seed only. Jellyfin reads logging.json if present and falls back to
logging.default.json otherwise; it never rewrites this file, so unlike
the two XML seeds this one stays authoritative.
One change from the shipped default: the Console sink is held at
Warning while the File sink stays at Information.
Why. Under --service, console output is stdout, and launchd sends
stdout to /var/log/jellyfin-server.launchd.log. At Information that
file becomes a byte-for-byte duplicate of the real log in
/var/log/jellyfin/ — which Jellyfin already rotates itself (daily, 3
retained). Duplicating it costs nothing in disk but a lot in signal:
the launchd log is where an operator looks when the daemon will not
start, and a startup failure is invisible in a thousand lines of
scheduled-task chatter. Held at Warning it is ~6 lines per start
instead of ~214, which is small enough to read at a glance.
Measured, so the baseline is known: those six are five MediaEncoder
warnings about CUDA/VAAPI/Vulkan filters that no Apple silicon build
has, plus one StaticFileMiddleware note about a missing ASP.NET
wwwroot that does not apply because -w passes the web client
explicitly. They recur on every start and are not a problem. First
start adds EF Core migration warnings which do not recur.
The full-detail log is not lost, it just lives in one place:
/var/log/jellyfin/log_*.log.
